Incremental document ingestion would not by itself demonstrate compatibility after normalization-rule or vocabulary changes.","This proposal is conditional: joint-project willingness is open, but Dragić’s start date and time allocation are unconfirmed and his stated capacity is limited."],"proposedActions":["Propose a six-month experiment using permission-cleared query-response data, knowledge-base snapshots and fresh bank-client queries. LinguaBot would provide Elasticsearch integration and linguist review; Dragić would design normalization and analysis. Verify separate tuning/evaluation samples against duplicate-query, session and temporal leakage. On tuning data, compare the existing baseline, Serbian morphology alone, phoneme canonicalization alone, and both together, holding corpus and ranking fixed; test preprocessing order separately. Freeze the best configuration, whichever it is. Go/no-go would require a below-5% miss rate on an independent held-out sample from the original bank population, separately before and after vocabulary updates, with the upper 95% confidence bound below 5%. Require working Elasticsearch integration, zero full-index rebuilds during updates, agreed precision/latency/maintenance limits, tooling/data costs within approximately EUR 8,000, and a testable prototype within six months. Missing evidence means no pass. Separately evaluate telecom transfer, Serbian inflections, new product names and within-word mixing.","Propose linguist review of every evaluation query at an agreed retrieval depth. Count one miss per submitted query instance when no returned answer is useful; use all evaluated query instances as denominator, retaining repeated submissions and counting unresolved judgments as misses. Report bank and telecom results separately. Treat existing query-response labels as provisional until relevance is validated; use controlled variants only as diagnostic tests.","Propose month one for permissions, baseline replication and split auditing; months two–three for the comparison; months four–five for untouched evaluation and vocabulary-update replay; month six for review. Log update time, linguist hours, precision and latency under agreed load. Test query-time expansion or compatible incremental updates without assuming either works. Agree numeric maintenance and precision/latency limits before testing; clarify research fees and infrastructure funding separately."],"questions":["Can Dragić confirm his start date, time allocation and interest in this scoped joint project, and can LinguaBot identify implementation and maintenance owners?","Can LinguaBot authorize anonymized queries, corresponding knowledge-base snapshots and logs for research, confirm usable relevance labels, and provide independent bank and telecom evaluation data under agreed processing restrictions?","What defines a useful result and retrieval depth, and what numeric precision, latency, load and maintenance limits should govern acceptance?","Which Elasticsearch configuration and update mechanisms are permitted without a full re-index, and how will tooling/data costs, research fees, compute and staff time be funded?"],"benefits":{"company":"The experiment could identify which normalization changes reduce real support-search misses and whether vocabulary updates remain practical without rebuilding the full index.","researcher":"Subject to agreement and permissions, the project could provide support-query material for studying morphology–script interactions and transfer beyond legal and news retrieval."}}
issues.explanation: constraint "The evaluation must test the company's below-5% miss-rate objective and ongoing maintenance burden rather than treating either as an assured outcome." has no source cited in facts; add a fact with the source recordId "C009-CH1", field "detail", quote "A good outcome is getting that 18% miss rate below 5% and keeping it there with a manageable maintenance process."

issues.claim: Proposed diagnostic go/no-go requires repeated reproduction of the field crack location and morphology at representative 2–10 °C exposure
issues.explanation: The company states its cold stores run at 2–5 °C, so calling 2–10 °C 'representative' allows acceptance testing above the service range and weakens the reproduction criterion; the fact list already uses 2–5 °C, and the acceptance exposure should be aligned with that stated range.
